source.check: every figure read twice, independently, from the BNA page images (blind double entry, reconciled; the two entries disagreed on no figure); the counts are checked against the valid poll and quota the paper prints; the full names of the unsuccessful candidates are from the list of candidates printed on polling day; the members as the council's minute lists them

note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919: the first county council election in the five electoral areas that replaced the county electoral divisions of 1899, 21 seats. Polled Thursday 3 June 1920 (Belfast News-Letter, 3 June 1920, p. 6, "To-day's Polling"); counted at the Courthouse, Crumlin Road, Belfast, by Alexander Millar, secretary of the county council, as returning officer. Ballymoney area (four seats): 8,412 valid votes, 352 spoiled, quota 1,683; 13,299 electors. First preferences only; the paper describes the transfers without figures. Stuart's votes were transferred first, then those of M'Mullan, Montgomery and M'Alister, and Walsh reached 1,821 on the fifth count; his surplus and the votes of Black and M'Auley were then distributed, and Watt (1,824), Keers (1,809) and Leslie (1,619) were declared elected on the eighth count. Walsh's and Watt's first preferences are partly illegible on the page (printed "1,4?7" and "1,?05", the latter struck through by a rule); 1,487 and 1,305 are the only readings that make the first preferences add to the valid poll. The first-count list prints "F. Walsh, 732": no Walsh other than the elected one stood, and Francis Black, junior, of Carnealty, is the only candidate it otherwise omits, so the figure is filed as his. It prints the elected Walsh as "R. J. Walsh" (Louis J. Walsh in the minute) and M'Alister as "Samuel"; the list of candidates on polling day gives Daniel Macalister, of Cushendall. Major J. A. Montgomery D.L. and Francis Black, junior, retiring members, were defeated. The minute of the council's first meeting also records the chairmen of the rural district councils, who sat ex officio, and the co-opted members; they were not elected and are not listed here.
sourceNote: Reading uncertain (owner review, 12 November 2026): the first-count list prints "F. Walsh, 732", filed as Francis Black, the only candidate the list otherwise omits; and it prints "Samuel M'Alister", filed as Daniel M'Alister (Daniel Macalister, of Cushendall, in the list of candidates on polling day). The clearer reading is kept in each case.
